RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 20

That number is a speculative, low-confidence judgment—not a statistically supported estimate. An all-women panel alone is not evidence of sex discrimination.

Your qualifications justify asking how the candidates were assessed, but the announcement may omit relevant experience, and interviews may legitimately affect rankings.

Follow up now on your written request. Ask for the selection criteria, assessment of your application, reasons for the appointment, and applicable review deadlines.

Raise panel composition neutrally if local rules require gender balance or other evidence suggests bias. A composition-rule breach would not itself prove discriminatory selection. Your stronger initial focus is whether the stated criteria were applied consistently. Legal rights and response deadlines depend on jurisdiction.
